newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Heavy casualties seen in Sri Lanka rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Heavy casualties seen in Sri Lanka rebel attack.

text.p: Heavy casualties were expected on both sides after Sri Lankan Tamil rebels attacked a key army- held northern town in the new year's first major battle, security forces officials in the area said on Thursday.

The pre-dawn attack on Paranthan, on the mainland just south of the Jaffna peninsula, was continuing well into the day, nearly 10 hours after Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas stormed the the northern junction town, they said.
"Both sides are still firing at each other. But reinforcements have gone in and essentially taken control of the situation," one military official told Reuters.
An LTTE spokesman contacted in London by Reuters had no comment on Thursday's attack.
Bodies of soldiers and rebels were seen in several places as government reinforcements, backed by air force helicopter gunships, began assessing the damage, other military officials said.
Casualty figures were not immediately available.
A Ministry of Defence statement said government soldiers had successfully repulsed the attack.
"The LTTE is withdrawing its cadres now, by boat and by land towards the east (of Paranthan)," the statement said.
A large number of guerrillas had penetrated the town's defences shortly after midnight and bombarded its military positions with artillery and mortars, military officials said.
A number of rebel suicide bombers also took part in the opening attack, they added.

Paranthan, (280 km) 185 miles north of the capital Colombo, sits astride the main north-south highway from Colombo to Jaffna and controls the road junction connecting to the rebel-held northeastern town of Mullaitivu.

Government forces, which captured Paranthan from the rebels last July, pushed further into rebel territory shortly afterwards to take control of Kilinochchi in August, the last major town controlled by the rebels.
"Our lines are stretched thin in this area. So it's a little easier to attack," one military official said.

The LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, were driven out of their Jaffna peninsula stronghold by government forces in April last year.
Officials said rebels had also fired artillery towards the Elephant Pass army camp, about four km (six miles) north of Paranthan on the neck of the peninsula, but they caused no damage.

Paranthan is the first military base to be attacked by the rebels this year. The LTTE overran a police commando camp at Pulukunawa in the eastern Amparai district in early December, killing 36 security personnel.
In July last year, the rebels overran a key army base at northeastern Mullaitivu, killing or capturing more than 1,000 men, dealing the military its biggest blow in the war, now in its 14th year.

Earlier this week, the rebels said they killed at least eight soldiers in a separate attack on Tuesday night on the army's northern forward defences in Vavuniya district, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Colombo.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
